texts.preamble: Priyanka R vs Jayaram H N on 17 November, 2025 Kabc020048842024 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (Scch-23) Dated This The 17th Day Of November - 2025 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani B.Com. Ll.B (Spl), Xxi Addl.
texts.facts: The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 04.10.2023 at about 10.00 a.m, when the petitioner in MVC.816/2024 was proceeding as pedestrian by the side of the road at Vaddarahalli, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, the driver of an car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913 came from Madanayakanahalli at high speed in a rash & negligent manner without observing the traffic rules, dashed against the petitioner in MVC.816/2024 from the back side and also dashed to the petitioner in MVC.817/2024 as she was standing by the side of the road. Due to the impact both the petitioners were fell on the road and sustained injuries all over the body. After the accident the petitioners were shifted to respective hospitals, treated accordingly and then discharged. They were still under treatment and had spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance Priyanka R vs Jayaram H N on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157792133/ 2 and other incidental expenses. On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement. 4 SCCH-23 MVC.816/2024 C/w MVC.817/2024 The respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation. 3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal. Hence he was placed exparte. 4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement and specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. It is specifically stated that the alleged accident caused by Maruti Vitara Breeza car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-ML-3913. However, their insured vehicle is bearing No.KA-41-MC-3913 and hence insured vehicle was not involved in the accident and the petitioner may be put to strict proof of the same. This respondent further admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913. However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy. Further 5 SCCH-23 MVC.816/2024 C/w MVC.817/2024 this respondent denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle and contended that the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioners as they walked on the road instead of footpath provided for the safety of Priyanka R vs Jayaram H N on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157792133/ 3 pedestrians and the police without proper investigation appears to have fixed the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC- 3913 for the alleged accident. Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913 did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident. Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. On these grounds prayed for dismissal of the petitions. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues (which are common in both petitions) were framed: ISSUES 1. In order to prove its defence the respondent No.2 insurance company examined the Investigating Officer as RW.1.
